source.title: Unique Properties of Flat Minima in Deep Networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures Hessian sharpness and studies flat minima, but does not measure the train-test generalization gap or test whether sharpness tracks it. Its discussion of generalization draws on cited prior work.
record.gate_note: The reported sharpness, gain, and training-loss results do not measure any listed version’s named generalization behavior. The paper’s generalization-related statements in the introduction and related work are claims or citations, not results testing the versions.
record.test_reason: The study characterizes Hessian sharpness and layer structure. Its SGD–Adam comparison reports training and validation losses for fully connected MNIST denoisers, outside V4's classification and language benchmarks. It does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure in a convolutional family.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors prove that flattest minima in linear networks with quadratic loss have restrained intermediate gains and coupled layers, and illustrate related properties in nonlinear MNIST denoisers. They also show that interpolation plots can misrepresent sharpness. They do not establish magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies sharpness and structure of minima in linear networks with quadratic loss, plus denoising experiments on nonlinear ReLU networks; it does not test the listed generalization claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization, optimizer, step size, and network depth change the measured sharpness or convergence behavior in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: For six-layer fully connected MNIST denoisers, SGD had lower Hessian sharpness (1.76 versus 12.9), training loss (0.0269 versus 0.0274), and validation loss (0.0270 versus 0.0280) than Adam. The corresponding mean validation-minus-training gaps are approximately 0.0001 and 0.0006.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this denoising setup, the tested SGD recipe reaches flatter solutions with lower validation loss and a smaller mean validation-minus-training gap than the tested Adam recipe.

record.problems: The nonlinear experiments concern MNIST denoising, not classification generalization. Sharpness is measured by the maximal Hessian eigenvalue, and no train-test gap is reported. Several plotted comparisons provide no exact numeric values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure-only sharpness values across depth and step size (Figures 4–5), and intermediate-gain comparisons (Figure 6), are not included because they do not report a generalization-gap outcome. The table provides the optimizer comparison rows retained above.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out classification accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance on classification or language benchmarks under specified tuning budgets, and the listed recovery strategies.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking of generalization gaps within a convolutional family, including comparison with norm and margin measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates the absence of generalization information: Table S1 reports validation losses alongside training losses, permitting calculation of mean validation-minus-training gaps. Those results still do not measure V7's named sharpness construct or system family. The paper's discussion of sharpness and generalization, including reparameterization arguments from prior work, does not independently test V7.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Test-error comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Held-out performance under large and small batches.
No train-test gap or magnitude-aware perturbation measure is reported; the paper measures maximal Hessian eigenvalue.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.uncertainty: Table S1 reports ± 9.43 × 10−3 for SGD and ± 2.2 for Adam.
rows.locator: Section 6, Figure 6 discussion; Supplementary Table S1
rows.note: The paper states the SGD minima had roughly 6× lower eigenvalue. This compares sharpness, not train-test gap.
rows.check: The numbers match Table S1, but lower maximal Hessian eigenvalue alone cannot establish any listed generalization effect. Change observed to cannot_determine. The table's mean eigenvalues differ by approximately 7.3×; roughly 6× is the main text's description.
